'''Ousmane Dieng''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|uː|s|m|ɑː|n|_|ˈ|dʒ|ɛ|ŋ}} ''{{respell|OOSS|mahn|_|JENG}}''; born 21 May 2003) is a French professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). After playing 3 years in France and New Zealand, Dieng was selected in the [[2022 NBA draft]] with the 11th overall pick by the [[New York Knicks]], but was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] on draft night. During the [[2024–25 NBA season|2024–25 season]], Dieng won his first [[NBA Finals|NBA Championship]] with the Thunder.

==Early life and youth career==
Dieng grew up in [[Lot-et-Garonne]] in southwestern France. His father Ababacar, originally from Senegal, was a former professional basketball player in France.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ousmane Dieng va jouer pour une équipe néo-zélandaise|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Basket/Actualites/Ousmane-dieng-va-jouer-pour-une-equipe-neo-zelandaise/1258233|work=[[L'Équipe]]|date=2 June 2021|access-date=2 June 2021|language=French}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Ousmane Dieng, the 20-Year-Old Philanthropist {{!}} Oklahoma City Thunder |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/ousmane-dieng-the-20-year-old-philanthropist |website=www.nba.com |language=en}}</ref>

At the youth level, Dieng played for Villeneuve Basket Club and [[JSA Bordeaux Basket|JSA Bordeaux]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Le Villeneuvois Ousmane Dieng en route pour la NBA|url=https://www.ladepeche.fr/2020/12/01/le-villeneuvois-ousmane-dieng-en-route-pour-la-nba-9230351.php|work=[[La Dépêche du Midi]]|date=1 December 2020|access-date=2 June 2021|language=French}}</ref> He attended the national athletics boarding school [[INSEP]] in [[Paris]], and competed for its under-18 team at the [[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|Next Generation Tournament]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Christophe|last=Cibola|title="La NBA est un objectif"|url=https://www.petitbleu.fr/2020/12/17/la-nba-est-un-objectif-9262265.php|work=Le Petit Bleu d'Agen|date=17 December 2020|access-date=2 June 2021|language=French}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Centre Fédéral (2020–2021)===
In the 2020–21 season, Dieng averaged 12.6 points, 5.8 rebounds, and 2.9 assists per game for [[Centre Fédéral de Basket-ball|Centre Fédéral]] in the [[Nationale Masculine 1]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Projected 2022 Lottery Pick Ousmane Dieng Becomes NBL Next Star with Breakers|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/projected-2022-lottery-pick-ousmane-dieng-becomes-nbl-next-star-with-breakers|website=NBL.com.au|publisher=[[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]]|date=1 June 2021|access-date=2 June 2021}}</ref>

===New Zealand Breakers (2021–2022)===
On 1 June 2021, Dieng announced that he would play for the [[New Zealand Breakers]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) in the [[2021–22 NBL season|2021–22 season]], alongside fellow Frenchman and eventual [[2022 NBA draft]] selection [[Hugo Besson]]. He became the first European player to join the league's Next Stars program to develop [[NBA draft]] prospects. Dieng had also been recruited by major [[college basketball]] programs and the [[NBA G League Ignite]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Adrian|last=Wojnarowski|authorlink=Adrian Wojnarowski|title=French 2022 NBA draft prospect Ousmane Dieng to play for New Zealand Breakers in NBL|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31547592|work=[[ESPN]]|date=1 June 2021|access-date=2 June 2021}}</ref> Dieng left the Breakers on 17 April 2022 in order to prepare for the [[2022 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dieng, Besson Turn Attention to NBA Draft|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/dieng-besson-turn-attention-to-nba-draft|website=NBL.com.au|date=17 April 2022|access-date=17 April 2022|archive-date=17 April 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220417074027/https://nbl.com.au/news/dieng-besson-turn-attention-to-nba-draft|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Oklahoma City Thunder / Blue (2022–2026)===
Dieng was selected with the eleventh overall pick by the [[New York Knicks]] in the [[2022 NBA draft]], and was then immediately traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in exchange for three [[2023 NBA draft|2023 first-round draft]] picks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Drafts Chet Holmgren, Ousmane Dieng, Jalen Williams and Jaylin Williams in the 2022 NBA Draft|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-draft22-220624|website=NBA.com|date=24 June 2022|access-date=24 June 2022}}</ref> On 15 April 2024, he won the [[NBA G League]] title with the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] and was named the [[NBA G League Finals Most Valuable Player Award|championship game most valuable player]] after getting 25 points, six boards, four assists and two blocks in the win against the [[Maine Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Oklahoma City Blue Wins First-Ever G League Championship|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/oklahoma-city-blue-win-2024-nba-g-league-finals|website=NBA.com|date=15 April 2024|access-date=16 April 2024}}</ref>

Throughout his first three seasons, Dieng has been [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2022–2023 Oklahoma City Blue Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Oklahoma-City-Blue/38/Transaction_History/2023|website=RealGM.com|access-date=21 December 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=2023–2024 Oklahoma City Blue Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Oklahoma-City-Blue/38/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=21 December 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=2024–2025 Oklahoma City Blue Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Oklahoma-City-Blue/38/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=21 December 2024}}</ref>

In the [[2024–25 NBA season]], Dieng appeared in 37 games, as Oklahoma City clinched its first-ever NBA championship with a victory over the [[2024–25 Indiana Pacers season|Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ousmane Dieng 2024–25 Stats per Game – NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4997526/ousmane-dieng |access-date=2025-10-07 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> Dieng played in 27 games for Oklahoma City during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], averaging 3.7 points, 1.6 rebounds, and 1.0 assist.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ousmane Dieng 2025–26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4997526/ousmane-dieng|access-date=March 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2026–present)===
On 4 February 2026, Dieng was traded with a 2029 second round pick to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in exchange for [[Mason Plumlee]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hornets Acquire Ousmane Dieng And 2nd Round Pick From Thunder |url=https://hornets.com/news/hornets-acquire-ousmane-dieng-and-2nd-round-pick-from-thunder |access-date=2026-02-04 |website=hornets.com |language=en}}</ref> Later in the day, Dieng, [[Collin Sexton]], and three second-round draft picks were traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in exchange for [[Coby White]] and [[Mike Conley Jr.]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/chicago-bulls-acquire-collin-sexton-ousmane-dieng-and-three-second-round-picks|title=CHICAGO BULLS ACQUIRE COLLIN SEXTON, OUSMANE DIENG AND THREE SECOND-ROUND PICKS|work=NBA.com|date=4 February 2026}}</ref> On 6 February, Dieng was traded again to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in a trade that also involved the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Milwaukee Bucks Acquire Ousmane Dieng In Three-Team Trade |url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-acquire-ousmane-dieng-in-three-team-trade |access-date=2026-02-06|date=2026-02-05 |website=bucks.com |language=en}}</ref> In his Bucks debut on 11 February, he scored 17 points and made a career-high five three-pointers made during a 116–108 win over the [[2025–26 Orlando Magic season|Orlando Magic]].<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7037331/2026/02/18/ousmane-dieng-bucks-nba-trade-thunder-hornets-bulls/ Ousmane Dieng was traded to 3 teams within hours. He’s since been a Bucks ‘jewel’]</ref> On 1 April, Dieng put up a career-high 36 points, along with 10 assists, in a 119-113 loss to the [[2025–26 Houston Rockets season|Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/bucks-ousmane-dieng-logs-career-highs-in-win/|title= Bucks' Ousmane Dieng: Logs career highs in win|website=CBS Sports|date=April 1, 2026|access-date=April 2, 2026}}</ref> He made 30 appearances (including 20 starts) for Milwaukee, recording averages of 11.0 points, 4.6 rebounds, and 3.6 assists (all career–highs).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ousmane Dieng 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4997526/ousmane-dieng|access-date=August 6, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

On 30 June 2026, Dieng re-signed with Milwaukee on three-year, $17.5 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 30, 2026 |title=Reports: Ousmane Dieng to re-up with Bucks on 3-year contract |url=https://www.nba.com/news/reports-ousmane-dieng-re-sign-bucks |access-date=July 5, 2026 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

==National team career==
Dieng represented [[France national under-17 basketball team|France]] at the [[2019 FIBA U16 European Championship]] in Italy. He averaged 8.9 points, 3.6 assists and 2.7 rebounds per game, helping his team win the silver medal.<ref>{{cite web|first=Evan|last=Daniels|title=French star Ousmane Dieng gaining high major interest|url=https://247sports.com/Article/Ousmane-Dieng-Arizona-Cincinnati-Oregon-State-Washington-State-147883567/|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=5 June 2020|access-date=2 June 2021}}</ref>
